identity.title: Identifiability of Deep Polynomial Neural Networks

problem.claim: The paper studies when deep Polynomial Neural Networks (PNNs), with or without bias terms, are identifiable.

gap.claim: Identifiability of PNNs, described as important for interpretability, remains poorly understood.

contributions.claim: A comprehensive identifiability analysis for deep PNN architectures with and without bias terms.
Constructive proofs connecting deep PNNs to low-rank tensor decompositions and Kruskal-type uniqueness theorems.
A resolution of an open conjecture about PNN neurovariety dimension, together with new bounds on activation degrees needed to attain the expected dimension.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a comprehensive analysis, constructive proof strategy, conjecture resolution, and new activation-degree bounds for deep PNN identifiability and dimension.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that identifiability depends on an intricate interaction between activation degrees and layer widths.
They report generic identifiability for architectures with non-increasing layer widths under mild conditions.
They report identifiability for encoder-decoder networks when decoder widths do not grow too rapidly relative to activation degrees.

narrative_sequence.summary: PNNs have rich algebraic and geometric structure, but their identifiability is poorly understood and relevant to interpretability.
The work analyzes identifiability in deep PNNs both with and without bias terms.
The reported results emphasize the interaction between activation degrees and layer widths.
Generic identifiability is reported for non-increasing widths under mild conditions and for encoder-decoder designs with sufficiently controlled decoder growth.
Constructive tensor-decomposition proofs support the analysis, alongside a reported conjecture resolution and activation-degree bounds for expected neurovariety dimension.

source_observation.claim: The abstract ties identifiability conclusions to explicit architectural quantities—activation degrees and layer widths—and states separate conditions for non-increasing and encoder-decoder widths.

lessons.interpretation: Claims about structural properties become more informative when organized around measurable design parameters and conditional regimes.
lessons.application: When presenting a theory result, partition the theorem or summary by architecture and state the controlling parameter relationship for each regime.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the result has no meaningful architectural parameters or when the abstract cannot specify the conditions governing each regime.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the mild conditions for generic identifiability or quantify how slowly decoder widths may grow.
Definitions of identifiability, neurovarieties, activation degree, and expected dimension are not provided.
The abstract does not state the exact conjecture, bounds, tensor assumptions, or proof scope beyond the summarized claims.
